{"id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-9098.34","title":"metrics.py: _tx_latency_recorded unbounded after 9098.24 caps","description":"## Problem

9098.24 capped `_delivered` (OrderedDict LRU 10k), `_collision_keys` (same), and `_time_series` (deque maxlen 10k), and stopped pruning undelivered `_tx_start_times` before 180 s so LatencyRule/90 s hops still record latency.

It did **not** cap or TTL `_tx_latency_recorded: set[str]`. That set is written on every first latency sample (`record_reception`) and is only cleared in `reset()`. The start-time prune *uses* it to choose the 60 s vs 180 s cutoff:

```python
if k in self._tx_latency_recorded:
    if v < delivered_cutoff:      # 60s
        old_keys.append(k)
elif v < undelivered_cutoff:      # 180s
    old_keys.append(k)
for k in old_keys:
    del self._tx_start_times[k]
# _tx_latency_recorded is not pruned
```

After a tx_id is deleted from `_tx_start_times`, its entry in `_tx_latency_recorded` is dead weight. Long runs therefore keep one string per historically delivered TX forever — the same class of leak 9098.24 closed for `_delivered`.

`test_delivered_and_time_series_are_capped` asserts `_delivered` and `_time_series` bounds only. Reservoir sampling (`_latency_samples`) is already capped. This set is the remaining unbounded companion of `_tx_start_times`.

This is not 9098.24 (those three collections + 60 s prune dropping delayed latency). It is not 9098.27/30 (RNG). After the 24 fix, the latency-recorded set is the prune oracle and is never aged.

## Files

- python/src/lichen/sim/metrics.py (`_tx_latency_recorded` add in `record_reception`; prune in `record_transmission_start`; `reset`)
- python/tests/sim/test_metrics.py (`test_delivered_and_time_series_are_capped`, `test_delayed_reception_keeps_latency_after_threshold`)

## Why this is robustness

9098.24's design was "do not grow without bound." City-mesh / soak / 500-node demo will record far more than 10k distinct tx_ids. The prune already forgets start times; leaving the classification set behind reintroduces unbounded growth on the metrics object that radio.py hits on every TX/RX.
